source: After you've left this world, that is.
And of course, to offer our sincere and heartfelt advice on these matters.
Not that we have the final say in anything.
Indeed. It's all up to you, love.
Consider this a temporary space to explore what has been and might be.
...So this is...
...This is some kind of... curtain call?
And if I leave here... then... all of this... will be over?
Time will move forward—and this will—be my fate?
Yes, that would seem to make good sense.
...Or, Option B, you could just stop thinking about it so hard.
I hate those people at the theater. Always scrutinizing everything to death.
We're all here to see you off. Even the dead are here. Isn't that enough?
The dead?
Indeed. For a small while, the Book of Fates can make even this miracle possible.
Then I won't waste this chance, everyone.
I'm going to make the best decision I can.
Marvelous. Let's get to it.
Aah, she's here, she's here!
Places, everyone! Please! It's time for the final curtain call!
If you'll allow me, I shall set the scene.
When we last left Ophelia, she was ready to use the Book of Fates to end her life.
What say you about this, friends?
I'm opposed, of course.
As am I. Ophelia, how could you even think of leaving us like that?
I love you. I want you to live on. I can't imagine a complete life without you.
Oh, you can't imagine life without her? You, who would leave her to gallivant around Paris?
Forty thousand brothers could not, with all their quantity of love, make up my sum—
Stop that, lads. Stop bickering. Need everything be a competition with you two?
...Ophelia, dear heart, you already know my thoughts.
To think of losing you the way I lost your mother—it would crush me.
I'm certain I couldn't survive it.
You are one of the few good things in our life. In all of our lives.
Things might seem dark now. But isn't there another way, my love? Surely there must be.
You're wrong.
I understand why you're saying this, Polonius. But you're wrong.
You know exactly what you're doing, don't you, Ophelia?
If you were to die...
Then one by one, the next pieces fall. Your brother gets his revenge. The Danish throne begins to implode. Hamlet dies.
Everything goes to ruin.
But the way things are now, in this country—it's festering from the inside. You see a side of it we don't.
If you die, then that allows something new to be born. That's why I was sent to kill you once.
To be frank, that's a future we should all be grateful for.
But what is a future like that worth if Ophelia must suffer for it?
She has done nothing wrong. She is innocent.
It doesn't matter. She's the only one who can die to create this fate.
My husband and I will suffer, too. This is a death sentence for us, Ophelia.
It's true we... weren't always good. Both of us did things we aren't proud of.
But if what Brit's saying is true, is it right that you condemn us to death for it?
You have the choice to save us. I don't want to die! I want to live and find a way to be good!
My wife speaks the truth. Choosing this ending leaves me with no path to redeem myself.
Nor Hamlet.
Yes. Although death is what I wished for, once--in my heart I've always been uncertain.
What if I was meant to live? What if there are greater things I could do for this world than to die?
If you choose this fate, I'll never get to find out.
This was the fate I brought upon myself by virtue of my inaction, once.
I did not know I had a choice to make at the time. I never found the Book of Fates. But in my heart of hearts, I chose it all the same.
If this is the future you desire, choose it with intent, Ophelia.
Do not shy away from the world, as I did. Go into the darkness with strength. Go with purpose.
That is all.
Thank you, everyone.
I think I know what I ought to know, now.
When we last left Ophelia, she was ready to use the Book of Fates to become Queen of Denmark.
We recently announced the news to all at Elsinore.
Once the tide of war has receded, we'll make the leap from betrothal to wedding.
Admittedly, there will be some pushback, but... I believe there's ample standing here to make Ophelia my wife.
But she... is the reason I'm dead.
Were it not for you, Ophelia, I'd be with my husband.
I-- I know it is the birthright of a King that he have a Queen beside him.
And my husband might have come to you himself in time, it's true.
But you went to him and you ployed his affections in his moment of deepest despair, didn't you?
You knew what you were doing.
Yes, yes, that's certainly true! You played me like a fiddle!
We ought to both hope that the real me never uncovers what you did!
Yes, this was far from a healthy match. One might call it outright predatory on both ends.
Still, in spite of that, I think you'd make an excellent queen.
...He's right, you know.
I... don't think I can ever accept you marrying Claudius. I'll always be furious about that.
He murdered my father. And you sided with him. That makes you a monster. You're no better than he is.
But even despite that, as a ruler, you have something in you that I never did.
You will need to be ruthlessly determined if you intend to survive the damage my father's death left behind.
Well, I'm glad that I don't have to marry Hamlet or Claudius.
I was afraid my father would want to make a political match. And I came rather close.
Now the two of us may be wed.
I didn't think of that! Yes, hrm... yes... a delightful match, if her father is willing.
Under ordinary circumstances, he wouldn't be. But with Laertes' sister as the new Queen, things have shifted.
So thank you, Ophelia. Your decision might bring the two of us some happiness, at least.
Although I never knew for certain that Claudius was his brother's killer...
I always suspected it, in my heart of hearts. I don't know that I could ever live happy, seeing my daughter at his side.
It is strange, how these matters bear forth.
You are a source of myriad surprises. I would never have anticipated this.
It is not my place to pass judgement on this union. Nor is it Gertrude's, in the end.
After all, this is not our world any longer.
It belongs to the living. To you.
When we last left Ophelia, she was ready to use the Book of Fates to sail off on Grace O'Malley's stolen vessel.
I see. So you're leaving us.
If you go, Ophelia, the rest of them shall tear each other apart, I fear.
Without you, there's nothing good remaining in Elsinore. We will all surely die.
And I'm already dead in this world, or so traumatized by my experiences with Hamlet that I ask to leave Elsinore forever. There's no returning from that.
It's true. Every time, we are sent to sea because I tried to kill your father. Because I am too dangerous to contain.
Ophelia... why would you leave us in our darkest hour?
Are we so utterly worthless to you that you'd cast us aside for your own joy?
Even I must admit the thought is troubling.
Please. Don't abandon us.
Don't go, sister. We still need you.
Ophelia! What'd I miss?
What are you doing here?
Coulda asked myself that same question. But hell, here I am.
I hate bein' out 'ere on shore. I jes' feel useless.
Anyway. Off we go! C'mon!
Hold a moment. Ophelia has not consented to leave us behind yet.
And if she does, we shall all perish.
Oh, I see! This is such an interestin' quandary.
So yer options, Ophelia, are t' come with me an' set sail for a life of adventure...
Drinkin', fuckin', and pillagin' every island we come across, cartin' mountains of gold from secret cove to secret cove...
Seein' sights no man or woman has ever laid eyes on before...
Then retirin' with yer pile o' gold to the private castle of yer choosin'...
Or dyin' here like a dog with all o' these self-righteous, boring-as-boiled-chicken fools!
What an interesting, nuanced decision.
Don't you ever get tired o' strugglin' so much?
Seems t'me like it's time to look out for number one—to scratch yer own back for once.
It's not that simple, Grace. This is my family. These are people I've known my whole life.
This world requires me to leave the people I love to die by each other's hand, and to take Denmark down with them.
It is tempting to flee responsibility for the lives of those you love.
I sought to do the same.
No man or woman could lay blame with you.
But I fled, and I have spent every moment of consciousness since regretting the world I chose.
Whatever you choose—whatever fate you grant yourself—do not forget that you must live dreaming of the faces you left behind.
I love you, Ophelia.
As do I. With all my heart. A world without my little sister in it isn't one worth having.
Yes. What would we do without you?
I cannot imagine it. Not without great difficulty.
When we last left Ophelia, she was ready to use the Book of Fates to elope with Othello the barkeep.
You hardly know this man, Ophelia. How can you be certain you want to leave with him?
Oh, that's no matter to me. Why, my sister married a man she'd met but once as a child. It's very common!
In fact, perhaps the best matches are made between strangers.
There's room for the marriage to grow, you see.
I merely hope your heart is ready for the difficulties which lie ahead of you. Leaving your life behind is no small feat, my love.
The Queen is correct. Are you prepared for the burdens you might have to endure?
She'll be just fine. I'm certain of it.
After all, Ophelia's been no stranger to hardship lately!
If this is what you desire, then so be it.
Please, everyone, listen.
I know my origins are humble, my intentions unclear.
I have never been a man given to certainty and to stability. My life has woven its course through many ditches and peaks.
But... I love Ophelia. And I know it to be true to the core of everything in me.
Never before could I see that my life was weaving towards something.
But now, all roads lead to her. My old life has turned to ash. And I wish for nothing more.
Come with me, Ophelia. Take my hand.
Not so fast, Ophelia.
You've heard my warning, and yet you still explore this world.
